title: [VIC] Up to $200 Sports/Activity Vouchers for Kids (0-18 Year Olds) of Eligible Families @ Get Active Victoria
body:
Deal: [VIC] Up to $200 Sports/Activity Vouchers for Kids (0-18 Year Olds) of Eligible Families @ Get Active Victoria

[AnDyStYLe] To be eligible, your child/dependant must be aged 0 to 18 years old, live in Victoria, and one of the below:
Named on a Health Care Card AND Medicare Card.
Named on a Pensioner Concession Card AND Medicare Card.
Hold either a temporary, provisional or student visa, or be an undocumented migrant.
Reside in Victorian Care Services or kinship care.
For each eligible child, you can only apply for either one voucher OR one reimbursement in each round.
🙅‍♂️ and VIC only.

[A Banana4scale] The Victorian Department of Jobs, Skills, Industry and Regions designed the Get Active Kids Voucher Program around low-income assistance, using Health Care Cards and Pensioner Concession Cards as the main check.
Families on student, temporary, or expired visas cannot get Medicare or Centrelink concession cards. To keep those children from missing out on sport, the department created a special consideration pathway.
This setup lets families apply without a Medicare card or Centrelink reference number. It runs through a separate process that bypasses automated federal database checks, letting kids join local sports clubs without flagging immigration status.

[A Banana4scale] Targeted grants exist solely to remove financial barriers for children in low-income or vulnerable households.
Middle-income families access substantial tax-funded support through scaled programs like the Child Care Subsidy (CCS) and Family Tax Benefit (FTB).
Public funding for youth sports directly lowers long-term state costs in public health, mental health services, and youth diversion programs. Lower state expenditure benefits every taxpayer regardless of who gets the initial $200 grant.
